claims.statement: On the fixed eight-channel mass-action graph with source complexes C and 2C, the two strictly positive rate vectors r_A=(2,1,4,1), q_A=(4,1,10,1) and r_B=(1,4,1,2), q_B=(1,10,1,4) induce identical full CLE drift and covariance fields for every state x.
assumptions: For k=1,2,3,4 the channels are C→E+(4-k)S+kP and 2C→2E+(8-k)S+kP
Factorial-normalized source monomials are x_C and x_C^2/2
Both parameter vectors are strictly positive on the same eight-reaction graph
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact algebra; finite-checked with rational arithmetic
claims.novelty_boundary: The source-wise lifted signature criterion is source-reported in Faul-Hoessly-Xia Theorem 3.3(1). This finite witness instantiates its known moment-nullspace mechanism at two source monomials; no general theorem or priority claim is made.

costs.input: Known graph, species list, source normalization, and two exact rate vectors are supplied.
costs.computation: Exact moment and matrix comparison; Python standard-library script runs in under one second locally.
costs.data: No data are needed for the structural coefficient identity.

claims.falsifier: Any source-wise difference in M0, M1, or M2, or any inequality between the printed polynomial drift/covariance matrices, invalidates the claimed CLE collision.
claims.next_gate: Obtain an independent mathematical review of the derivation and verify that the factorial-normalized CLE convention matches the intended finite-volume chemical model.

claims.statement: For the finite CTMC initialized at (C,E,S,P)=(2,0,0,0), the complete product-jump path law differs between the two CLE-equivalent rate vectors. The exact CTMC likelihood-ratio test needs five independent runs for sum of type-I and type-II errors at most 0.05; endpoint product counts alone need sixteen runs for that criterion.
assumptions: Finite-copy propensities are r_k C for source C and q_k binom(C,2) for source 2C
Assays are independent and observed to completion
Only product-count jump sizes in {1,2,3,4} are observed; no reaction-source label is available
The two candidate rate vectors are known simple hypotheses
Readout has zero error and there are no background reactions
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact path and endpoint laws; likelihood errors and adjacent minimum counts finite-tested by exact integer/rational dynamic programming
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a two-source, state-dependent finite CTMC construction and a fixed-pair acquisition result, not an empirical discovery or a new general identifiability theorem. It does not include detector noise, rate-calibration cost, or finite-sample nuisance-rate estimation.

costs.marked_path: Five-run sum-error target uses ten prepared C intermediates, at most ten product-jump records (expected 7.5), and five completion checks if depletion is not directly observable. Four runs give equal conditional errors 0.0395544 each; five give 0.0249843 each.
costs.endpoint_only: Sixteen independent C=2 runs are needed for sum-error ≤0.05, each with one final product count in {1,...,8}; eleven runs suffice for equal-prior Bayes error ≤0.05.
costs.measurement: Resolve every event product-yield increment exactly as an integer 1 through 4 and run to completion; a calibrated analog readout rounded to the nearest integer needs absolute error below 0.5 molecule-equivalent. No practical detector noise model is supplied. Event timestamps carry no information for the fixed A-vs-B comparison.
costs.runtime: One run has expected completion time 3/32 time units. A fixed horizon T≥ln(500)/8 gives a union-bound batch censoring probability at most 1% for five runs.

claims.falsifier: An event yield outside 1..4, more than two events, persistence of C beyond the model's completion tail, or violation of C+E=2 or 4C+S+P=8 falsifies the closed pair. A larger batch with poor likelihood under both hypotheses rejects the pair rather than favoring one.
claims.next_gate: Validate the cooperative 2C chemistry, calibrate the product-jump observation channel and preparation state, then recompute the exact LRT with measured confusion and rate uncertainty.

claims.statement: For the fixed two-source graph and exact completed product-marked event-time law from a controlled C=2 initialization, all eight positive source rates are structurally identifiable even though their CLE rate map is not injective.
assumptions: The graph is known and source reactions follow the stated first- and second-order propensities
The output records event times, ordered product-yield increments, and completion/path length, but not chemical source or internal state
Rates are strictly positive and the event-time law is observed ideally
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact structural inversion; no finite-sample confidence or noisy acquisition result
claims.novelty_boundary: The result is specific to this small controlled hidden-source CTMC. It does not establish generic partial-observation identifiability for reaction networks.

costs.input: Controlled C=2 initial count and fixed reaction graph.
costs.observation: First waiting time identifies H=2R+Q; second gap on two-event paths identifies R; Q=H-2R; conditional marks identify normalized rates r/R and q/Q.
costs.limitation: If waiting times are discarded, common positive scaling of all rates leaves the marked-path law unchanged.

claims.falsifier: Two distinct positive (r,q) pairs producing the same ideal marked-time law would contradict the stated inversion; an exact symbolic counterexample is the decisive audit.
claims.next_gate: Derive finite-sample intervals or an optimal nuisance-rate acquisition policy under a calibrated noisy observation channel.

claims.statement: For a centered compound-Poisson process with unknown intensity and jump density observed on a coarse mesh Δ_T→∞ with T/Δ_T→∞ and T/Δ_T^2=o((log(T/Δ_T))^{-1/4}), Duval Theorem 2 gives a strictly positive local asymptotic minimax lower bound in the loss ||(λ,f)||_{2,P}=||λf||_2, so consistent estimation of (λ,f) is impossible when Δ_T is of order T^α for 1/2<α<1.
assumptions: The compound-Poisson jump law is centered, has finite variance, and is an unknown density f
The parameter r=(λ,f) lies in the paper's class P and r0 has finite stated L2,P norm
Observations are floor(T/Δ_T) independent increments over horizon T
Δ_T→∞, T/Δ_T→∞, and the paper's logarithmic condition holds
claims.status: source-reported primary theorem reconstructed from the author manuscript
claims.novelty_boundary: The result concerns asymptotic coarse-time sampling of stationary independent increments. It is not a finite-volume state-dependent CRN result and is distinct from the exact finite-count assay above.

costs.statistical: A fixed local parameter neighborhood has positive asymptotic minimax risk; the theorem is not a sample count for the catalytic pair.

claims.falsifier: A uniformly consistent estimator over one of the theorem's stated local neighborhoods under its mesh conditions would contradict the source-reported lower bound.
claims.next_gate: No new application is claimed; retain as a novelty-boundary reference only.
